source_caption: The production of 𝐏𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭 𝐁𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐤 (𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟏) began under the working title “Johnny Utah” following the casting of Keanu Reeves. The studio later changed the title to “Riders on the Storm” after the song by The Doors during the period Patrick Swayze joined the cast. Producers eventually rejected both titles due to a lack of perceived relevance to surfing and the lyrical content of the song. The final title, “Point Break,” was selected approximately halfway through principal photography. It describes a type of wave that breaks as it hits a point of land or a rock protrusion extending from the coastline, creating a long, consistent, and predictable ride favored by surfers.

source_details.title: Point Break
source_details.synopsis: Point Break is a 1991 American action film directed by Kathryn Bigelow and written by W. Peter Iliff. It stars Patrick Swayze, Keanu Reeves, Gary Busey and Lori Petty. The title refers to the surfing term "point break", where a wave breaks as it hits a point of land jutting out from the coastline. The film features Reeves as an undercover FBI agent who is tasked with investigating the identities of a group of bank robbers while he develops a complex relationship with the group's leader (Swayze). Development of Point Break began in 1986, when Iliff wrote an initial script for the film. Bigelow soon developed it with her husband, James Cameron, and filming took place four years later.
